clue.text: One in 20 teachers will admit abuse

indicators.note: the union will admit, or let in, the word for abuse, so it sits inside

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British teaching union
to dis someone is to abuse or insult them

explanation.surface: A tale of a teaching union in which one in twenty members confesses to misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle 20 stands for NOTHING, so 'One in 20' is one dressed in nothing. 'will admit' puts DIS inside NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes about unclothed is wearing no garments at all, so is in a state of undress.

clue.text: 20 conceals murder like it!

indicators.note: the word for nothing hides the slang for murder inside it

parts.note: 20 is NOTHING in this puzzle, and none means not any, nothing
to ice someone is gangster slang for murder

explanation.surface: Nothing hides a killing, says someone admiring the cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like it!' is not a simile but an exclamation of approval, and 20 stands for this puzzle's theme word.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is praise for a good joke or deed, said when you enjoy it.

clue.text: Ancient lawmaker turned up in old book

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a referee who books a player cards him, so to book is to card

explanation.surface: A lawgiver of antiquity was discovered in an old volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns O CARD round. 'book' looks like a noun but is the verb used of referees.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian legislator was notorious for harsh laws, hence 'draconian'.

clue.text: Notice pressure when gripping warm surface

indicators.note: the letters for notice and pressure hold the word for warm inside

parts.note: to see is to notice
warm and kind both describe a friendly nature
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Notice the pressure when your hand grips a hot surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' puts KIND inside SEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, both mean superficial, not going below the outer layer.

clue.text: Mother managed to swallow 20 cake ingredient

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: the word for managed takes in, or swallows, the word for nothing

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
20 is NOTHING in this puzzle, and zip is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Mum manages to eat a whole twenty of something used in baking.
explanation.walkthrough: As throughout this puzzle, 20 stands for the theme word, the solution at 20-down.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond paste is used to cover fruit cakes, especially at Christmas.

clue.text: Dipsomaniac's wasted time going in for relaxing treatment

indicators.note: the abbreviation for time is inserted into the scrambled letters
wasted, drunk, says the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the possessive is read as a plural, keeping its S

explanation.surface: A drunk's ruined time ends with him going into rehab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' scrambles DIPSOMANIACS into ANISPASMODIC and 'going in' inserts T.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that relieves muscle cramps relaxes the body.

clue.text: Ridiculously lazy in work

indicators.note: work as a verb means to shape or knead, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A lazy worker behaving absurdly on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' signals an anagram of LAZY IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting like a clown, in a comically silly way, is acting absurdly.

clue.text: Perhaps some kinky private nurses start to treat one

indicators.note: nurses means holds closely, so the jumbled letters cradle the other pieces
kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent out of order
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Kinky private nurses who begin to treat someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' turns PRIVATE into PARTIVE, and 'nurses' puts T (from 'start to treat') and I inside it. 'Perhaps' marks 'some' as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'some' denotes part of a whole, so it is a word of that class.

clue.text: Layer supporting 20 well!

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the one it holds up

parts.note: 20 is NOTHING in this puzzle, and nowt is northern English for nothing
a hen is a bird that lays eggs

explanation.surface: A hen holds up nothing, to general surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nowt' is northern English dialect for nothing. 'supporting' puts HEN below NOWT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections used to begin a remark or as a mild rebuke, as in 'come, come'.

clue.text: Sort of cable -flatter one, aluminium

parts.note: to coax someone is to win them over with flattery
I is the Roman numeral for one
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Advice on a cable: sweet-talk it, use one aluminium wire.
explanation.definitionFit: This type of cable has a central conductor inside a shared-axis shield, as used for TV aerials.

clue.text: Line agreed by the French 20 or, facetiously, the French king

parts.note: oui is French for yes
20 is NOTHING in this puzzle, and squat, as in diddly squat, is slang for nothing
taken as written
ze is a jokey mock-French way of saying the

explanation.surface: A line approved by the French, nothing or a jokey reference to their royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facetiously' marks ZE as a comic French accent for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis XIV, the Sun King, was the fourteenth ruler of that name in France.

clue.text: Series of notes plastered on tower

indicators.note: plastered suggests something drunk and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Musical notation daubed across the side of a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' signals an anagram of ON TOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: In twelve-tone music the composer fixes an ordering of all twelve pitches, the basis of the piece.

clue.text: Form close to 20 20 20

parts.note: 20 is NOTHING in this puzzle, and O, the zero figure, is nothing
a void is an emptiness, so nothing

explanation.surface: A bare string of twenties after the word for shape, a clue reading almost like a code.
explanation.walkthrough: With 20 meaning NOTHING, the definition is 'shape close to nothing', that is, shaped almost like the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg shape is nearly round, close to a circle or zero figure, so it is a form near to an O.

clue.text: Charitable company's withdrawn from advising swimmers

indicators.note: the company abbreviation is taken away from the word for advising

parts.note: to counsel is to advise
CO is the usual abbreviation for company
fish are creatures that swim

explanation.surface: A firm pulls out of giving advice to swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn from' removes CO from COUNSEL, leaving UNSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous, giving person puts others first rather than themselves.

clue.text: State means to construct American road

parts.note: to express is to state
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: A state plans how to build a highway in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage a highway for fast traffic with limited access is called this.

clue.text: Star has to write name using memory

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tag is a name or label
RAM is computer memory

explanation.surface: A celebrity must sign a name using her memory.
explanation.definitionFit: This five-pointed figure is a star shape, used as a magic symbol.

clue.text: With people around, left firing range?

indicators.note: the word for people is placed around the abbreviation for left

parts.note: kin are one's people, one's family

explanation.surface: A soldier on a shooting range left with others around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing range?' suggests guns, but it means an oven for firing pottery; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottery is fired in this oven, so it offers a range for firing in the baking sense.

clue.text: Met a radio presenter, one I'd abused

parts.note: a DJ, disc jockey, presents records on radio

indicators.note: abused means mistreated, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: Meeting a radio host whom one had treated badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' scrambles ONE I'D into OINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that touch at a boundary are next to each other, so they meet.

clue.text: Spots back part of hidden camera

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Spotting something at the back of a concealed camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' picks ENCA from 'hidden camera' and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin complaint shows itself as pimples, so a crop of pimples.

clue.text: Irrational fear about short crack in water bed

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about the shortened word
irrational means unreasoned, so the letters are rearranged
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a crack is a wisecrack, a quip

explanation.surface: An irrational fear about a short crack in a water bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water bed' suggests a mattress, but here it is a geological stratum holding water.
explanation.definitionFit: This underground layer of porous rock holds groundwater, a geological bed of water.

clue.text: Cold egg sandwiches vilified by beef lover?

parts.note: C is the usual abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the phrase for egg holds the word for vilified between its parts, like bread round a filling

parts.note: to egg on is to urge on
someone vilified finds that their name is mud

explanation.surface: A cold egg sandwich, scorned by a man who would rather have beef.
explanation.walkthrough: To beef is to grumble, so a 'beef lover' is a habitual complainer; the question mark flags the pun. 'sandwiches' puts MUD inside URGE ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad-tempered old grouch loves nothing more than having a moan.

clue.text: Worthless type of alcoholic drink with watery content

indicators.note: content, what is held, says the word for watery sits inside

parts.note: nog is a strong beer or egg-based drink
thin, like watery, means diluted

explanation.surface: A kind of alcoholic drink that is mostly water is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type of alcoholic drink' looks like one phrase, but 'Worthless type' is the definition, a person of no account.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of no importance is a nobody, a mere cipher.

clue.text: A 20 in graduate's paper

indicators.note: the A and nothing go inside the graduate's letters

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate
20 is NOTHING in this puzzle, and nil is nothing

explanation.surface: A zero mark on a graduate's essay.
explanation.walkthrough: The paper is a strong brown wrapping paper, not an exam script.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong brown wrapping paper is named after the hemp from the Philippine capital.

clue.text: Incompatible as initial in univers with 20pt Baskerville Bold endings

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter, here taken from the typeface name

parts.note: 20 is NOTHING in this puzzle, and nada is Spanish-derived slang for nothing; pt is taken as written

indicators.note: the final letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: Typography talk: Univers and Baskerville Bold at 20 point do not go together.
explanation.walkthrough: Univers and Baskerville are typefaces and pt is the point size. 'initial in' gives U, 20 gives NADA, pt gives PT, and 'endings' gives E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not altered to suit its setting is unfitted to it, so it fails to match.

clue.text: Had better tip off 20

indicators.note: the tip, or first letter, of the word for nothing is taken off

parts.note: 20 is NOTHING in this puzzle, and nought is nothing

explanation.surface: A warning: you had better pass on a tip-off to twenty people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip off' removes the first letter, N, of NOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: As a modal verb it expresses duty, as in 'you should go', the same as 'had better'.

clue.text: Kid on hand to make good 20

parts.note: 20 is NOTHING in this puzzle, and love is nothing in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A child to hand who makes good nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Kid here is goatskin leather, worn on the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid leather is used for fine gloves, so a kid on the hand is hand-wear.

clue.text: A blacksmith's 20 that is in basic education

parts.note: 20 is NOTHING in this puzzle, and FA, short for sweet Fanny Adams, is British slang for nothing

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes inside the three Rs

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are basic education
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A smith's nothing-to-speak-of learning, that is, just the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet Fanny Adams' is British slang for nothing at all; the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith who shoes horses is a specialist ironworker, so a type of blacksmith.

clue.text: Italian songs might, over in Australia

parts.note: can, like might, expresses possibility or ability

indicators.note: over says the phrase in Oz is turned round

parts.note: taken as written
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: Italian songs might be heard over in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the whole phrase 'in Oz' round, not just one word of it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lyrical Italian part-songs or ballads, the plural of an Italian word for song.

clue.text: Attendant breaking up Derby County riots

indicators.note: the attendant breaks into the nickname, splitting it apart

parts.note: the Rams is the nickname of Derby County football club
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: A steward splits up trouble involving Derby County football fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby County is an English football club nicknamed the Rams, hence the riots of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent sprees of uproar are disturbances like riots.

clue.text: Tennis player's energy, levels of noise and work

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
dB, decibels, measure noise levels
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A tennis star's energy, the noise he makes and his effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Stefan Edberg was a Swedish champion who won Wimbledon twice.
